- `evidence.verification` — the scope that WAS verified. `limited: true` =
  no artifact content was verified: only the database's stamp, and in git
  the commit, prove the release — say so plainly;
- `evidence.contract` — the version-file contract: `state: "unknown"`
  (nothing was ever confirmed) is not the same as a `"confirmed"` empty
  list;

and, beside the evidence, `details.executor` — the executor ASSIGNED to the
record now: a responsibility for its further handling (`provenance: false`),
not who made the release — and `details.finish`: the ways to finish a
release the evidence leaves at `committed`. Ask "Record this release" /
"Stop". Only on yes:

```bash
dct release reconstruct --version 1.0.0 --confirm --json
```

Outcome `reconstructed`. Refused → show the reason; the owner decides —
never reconstruct by hand, never write the record another way. The step for
each refusal and for finishing:

| situation | step |
| --- | --- |
| several verified candidates, no tag (`details.candidates`) | show them all; dct picks none — the owner picks one: `dct release reconstruct --version V --release-commit <sha> --json`, then the same with `--confirm` |
| the release commit changed older changelog history (`details.history`) | show the diff (`state`, `diff`, `diff_lines`); nothing is recorded and no flag or waiver exists — also for a typo fix; the release stays without a record |
| outside git, the contract is unknown (`details.contract`, `state: "unknown"`) | `dct release version-files --json` (outcome `none` = UNKNOWN, `found` = confirmed); ask the owner which files hold the version, or none; with THAT answer `dct release version-files --set <a,b> --confirm --json` or `dct release version-files --none --confirm --json` (outcome `confirmed`); then reconstruct again |
| the project's executor is `own` (`details.executor: "own"`) | its tool supplies the evidence file: `dct release reconstruct --version V --evidence <file.json> --json`, then the same with `--confirm` — the file comes from the own tool, never composed by this dialog |
| the record ends at `committed` (`details.finish`) | way `takeover` → the takeover of the **Resume path** above (preview, the owner approves that digest, resume); way `ledger` → whoever performs the missing tag and push records them (`docs/release-workflow.md#executor-k-85`; the only way for an `own` record) |

## Question count

A dialog is one AskUserQuestion; an answer is one question inside it. The
tests count answers (decisions), not dialogs. The "Details" question of a
screen longer than 15 lines is reading, not a decision, and is not counted.

| path | dialogs | answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typical, clean tree | 1 | 2 (Keep listed first, marked recommended) |
| Dirty tree (uncommitted changes) | 1 (+1 when a hook changes files or the state moves) | 2 |
| With all N (≤ 4 waiting) | 1 | 2 |
| Another version | 2 (the screen again) | 4 |
| Nothing proven, ≤ 4 waiting | 1 | 2 |
| Nothing proven, > 4 waiting | 2 (one question + screen) | 3 |
| First version | 1 | 1 (Q2 omitted: the screen shows the proposed version) |
| Change something | +1 dialog B and +1 screen per round | — |
| Finish an approved release | 1 (instead of the screen) | 1 |
| Unfinished record | 1 (instead of the screen) | 1 |
| Changelog file to settle | +1 before the screen | +1 |
| Version can't be read | +1 before the screen | +1 (Q2 then keeps the typed one) |
| Own release tool | 0 | 0 |

## Rules

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.
The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

- **The screen travels inside the dialog.** What the owner must read before
  answering is the preview of the option it belongs to, at most 15 lines as
  the dialog shows them. The dialog wraps long lines itself, about 60
  characters wide: a paragraph is one line, never broken by hand (a second
  break leaves single words on a line), and a list or table line stays under
  60 characters. Message text written before a dialog is never the screen: it
  can land in the thinking block, which the owner sees only as a one-line
  summary, so no question or option says "shown above". A longer screen is
  split into pages of at most 15 lines: the option's preview shows page 1, and
  one more single-select question, "Details", has one option per page (2 to
  4), each with that page as its preview; its answer is not a decision.

When a user decision is needed, use `AskUserQuestion`. Long text is in previews and Details pages, never in option labels or descriptions. A Details answer is reading, not approval.
- The owner decides on ONE screen; "Release" IS the yes. Nothing is
  committed, stamped, tagged or pushed before it, and the version released
  is the one the screen shows — dct's proposal listed first in Q2, changed
  there (a first version, which has no Q2: under "Change something").
- ALWAYS plan first and route from that ONE result (Step 1). An unfinished
  record is resumed or — on the owner's explicit decision — abandoned,
  never replaced by a new version; an unchanged resume needs no second
  question, a takeover and a changed scope need a new consent.
- An entry goes in only when a commit says it is done; "Release with all N"
  is never the first option.
- Never retry a refusal on your own and never loop on a lock — the one
  exception is the single automatic re-run of `apply --consent` after exit
  75 or an unreadable remote before the stamp ("The one automatic re-run");
  after it, a plain sentence and stop. Any further run waits for the owner
  ("run /release again").
- `dct release abandon` only with the owner's reason and explicit
  confirmation.
- Every refusal is one plain sentence with a true next step; identifiers
  only on the final "Technical details" line.
